sub_graphs.title: EIP-1559 Base Fee Mechanism
sub_graphs.description: Models the dynamic base fee pricing introduced in London fork

nodes.label: Parent Block Data Available
nodes.description: Parent block gas_used, gas_limit, and base_fee_per_gas are available

nodes.label: Calculate Target Gas
nodes.description: Compute target gas: parent_gas_limit / ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER (2)

nodes.label: Compare Usage to Target
nodes.description: Determine if parent gas_used equals, exceeds, or is below target

nodes.label: Usage at Target
nodes.description: Parent gas usage exactly equals target - base fee unchanged

nodes.label: Usage Above Target
nodes.description: Parent gas usage exceeds target - base fee increases

nodes.label: Usage Below Target
nodes.description: Parent gas usage below target - base fee decreases

nodes.label: Calculate Base Fee Increase
nodes.description: Increase base fee proportionally, max 12.5% (1/8) per block

nodes.label: Calculate Base Fee Decrease
nodes.description: Decrease base fee proportionally, max 12.5% (1/8) per block

nodes.label: New Base Fee Determined
nodes.description: Base fee for current block has been calculated

sub_graphs.title: London Transaction Type Processing
sub_graphs.description: Models the handling of legacy, EIP-2930, and EIP-1559 transaction types

nodes.label: Transaction Bytes Received
nodes.description: Raw transaction bytes received for decoding

nodes.label: Detect Transaction Type
nodes.description: Check first byte to determine transaction type (0x01, 0x02, or legacy RLP)

nodes.label: Legacy Transaction Detected
nodes.description: Transaction is legacy format (no type prefix)

nodes.label: Access List TX Detected
nodes.description: Transaction is EIP-2930 type (0x01 prefix)

nodes.label: Fee Market TX Detected
nodes.description: Transaction is EIP-1559 type (0x02 prefix)

nodes.label: Decode Legacy TX
nodes.description: RLP decode legacy transaction with gas_price

nodes.label: Decode Access List TX
nodes.description: Decode EIP-2930 TX with access_list field

nodes.label: Decode Fee Market TX
nodes.description: Decode EIP-1559 TX with max_fee and max_priority_fee

nodes.label: Calculate Effective Gas Price
nodes.description: For EIP-1559: min(max_priority_fee, max_fee - base_fee) + base_fee

nodes.label: Transaction Decoded
nodes.description: Transaction successfully decoded with effective gas price

external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
external_entities.description: User or application submitting transaction via JSON-RPC

sub_graphs.title: London Access List Gas Accounting
sub_graphs.description: Models the gas cost calculation for pre-declared storage access

nodes.label: TX with Access List
nodes.description: Transaction includes access_list with pre-declared addresses and storage keys

nodes.label: Count Access List Addresses
nodes.description: Count number of addresses in access list

nodes.label: Count Storage Keys
nodes.description: Count total storage keys across all addresses

nodes.label: Calculate Access List Gas
nodes.description: Compute: addresses * 2400 + storage_keys * 1900

nodes.label: Add to Intrinsic Gas
nodes.description: Add access list cost to TX_BASE_COST (21000) + data costs

nodes.label: Warm Accessed Addresses
nodes.description: Mark all access list addresses as 'warm' for reduced access cost

nodes.label: Warm Storage Slots
nodes.description: Mark all access list storage keys as 'warm' for reduced SLOAD cost

nodes.label: Access List Applied
nodes.description: Access list gas charged and slots pre-warmed

sub_graphs.title: London Gas Refund Mechanism
sub_graphs.description: Models the reduced 20% gas refund cap in London fork

nodes.label: TX Execution Complete
nodes.description: EVM execution finished with refund counter accumulated

nodes.label: Read Refund Counter
nodes.description: Get accumulated gas refund from SSTORE operations

nodes.label: Calculate Maximum Refund
nodes.description: Compute max refund: gas_consumed * 20% (reduced from 50%)

nodes.label: Take Minimum of Refund and Cap
nodes.description: Actual refund = min(refund_counter, max_refund)

nodes.label: Calculate Effective Gas Used
nodes.description: Effective = gas_consumed - actual_refund

nodes.label: Refund to Sender
nodes.description: Return (gas_limit - effective_gas_used) * effective_gas_price to sender

nodes.label: Gas Refund Complete
nodes.description: Sender has received refund for unused gas

ambiguities.text: The specification says base fee 'increases' or 'decreases' proportionally but does not specify exact rounding behavior
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume integer division is used (floor rounding) for base fee adjustments. This could cause drift over time.

ambiguities.text: INITIAL_BASE_FEE of 1 Gwei is mentioned but conditions for its application are not explicit
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume INITIAL_BASE_FEE is used only for the first London block and subsequent blocks use calculation.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly state what happens if max_fee_per_gas < base_fee
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume transaction is rejected as invalid if max_fee_per_gas is less than current base_fee.

implicit_assumptions.description: The ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER of 2 is assumed to provide sufficient flexibility for demand spikes
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Insufficient elasticity could cause severe fee spikes during high demand or block stuffing attacks

implicit_assumptions.description: The 12.5% maximum base fee change per block limits fee manipulation by miners/validators
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Faster fee changes could enable fee manipulation strategies by block producers

implicit_assumptions.description: The base fee portion is burned, reducing ETH supply
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If base fee is not burned, the economic model changes significantly with inflationary pressure

implicit_assumptions.description: Pre-warming addresses and storage via access lists correctly reduces cold access costs during execution
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect warm/cold accounting could lead to gas underpricing or overpricing of storage operations

implicit_assumptions.description: The 20% refund cap (down from 50%) is assumed to adequately prevent gas token arbitrage
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Higher refund cap could enable profitable gas token schemes that distort block space pricing
